text:
maya: dropping the first pass of the 'affirmation' modal for autoscale edits into figma: https://www.figma.com/file/DEF/autoscale-affirmation liam: skimmed 44d. I like the compact header. first major item: the cost line needs a clear timeframe and 'approx' marker. sara: copy thought: header -> 'Confirm autoscale change' and subhead -> 'This will change baseline capacity and burst behavior.' primary CTA 'Apply changes' secondary 'Provision now' (tiny helper text under CTA) ethan: accessibility checklist: focus moves into modal on open, focus trap enabled, ESC closes, use aria-live for the estimates block so screen readers hear updates. olivia: product ask: surface a top-line three-metric summary (cost delta, projected 99p latency delta, selected GPU pool) so users can make a quick call. maya: added the summary row. question: how should we treat burst when users set min equal to max? disable? warn? liam: strongly prefer disabling burst in that case and showing a concise tooltip that explains why. users shouldn't get a toggle that does nothing. sara: tooltip wording: 'Burst requires max > min. Increase max to allow short spikes without increasing baseline.' keeps it actionable. ben: pool selector idea: show inline pool chips with small icons, free GPUs count, and a latency-tier pill (low/med/high). favorite the pool that would be used for burst. kelsey: mobile constraint: pool chips need to wrap elegantly; consider a collapsible horizontal scroller or an overflow menu on small widths. ethan: implementation: debounce estimate API calls to 250ms when sliders change; cancel inflight requests; show skeletons in the summary cards while computing. liam: subtle UX: animate numerical deltas (count up) rather than jump cut to new values. also ensure numbers have units (ms, $/mo, GPUs). sara: microcopy tweak: change 'estimated cost impact' -> 'estimated monthly cost change (approx.)' and link to 'assumptions' which opens a tiny panel listing tokens/hr, avg seq len, region pricing. maya: on SLOs: show only estimates and label them clearly. no wording like 'guarantee' or 'will'. prefer 'expected 99p latency: 120ms -> 98ms (estimate)'. ben: guardrails: if the change reduces projected SLO below configured thresholds, show a yellow warning. if it violates a hard guardrail show red and require an extra confirmation checkbox. olivia: also show peak capacity estimate when burst is enabled: 'Projected peak QPS with burst: ~1.2k' so PMs can reason about traffic. kelsey: a11y nit: ensure all icon-only chips have aria-labels and target sizes 44px min. contrast ratios for latency pills need verifying. ethan: snippet to add to dev comments:
\n
Estimated monthly cost: $13.40
\n
liam: QA notes: test min==max, min>max inputs, selecting pools without burst support (should auto-disable burst), and simultaneous slider edits to ensure debouncing works. sara: copy for disabled-burst tooltip: 'Burst disabled because min equals max. Increase max to enable short spikes.' (reads clearer) ben: backend note: some pools are 'burst-incompatible' due to placement constraints. if user picks one, show inline helper 'selected pool cannot burst'. maya: visual layout decision: top summary row + expandable 'details' accordion. keeps modal compact but allows deep dives. olivia: acceptance criteria draft: - estimates compute <200ms median after debounce - skeleton shown while computing - disabled-burst shows tooltip and is non-interactive - pool chips collapse on mobile - acceptance tests for guardrails and pool capability. maya: action items: sara -> finalize microcopy; ben + kelsey -> responsive chips spec; ethan -> debounce + aria commit; liam -> animation + visual polish; olivia -> add telemetry checks for estimate accuracy. deploy-bot: uploaded image -> affirmation-modal-v1.png maya: thanks all. i'll update figma + add the acceptance criteria to the JIRA ticket and ping when the staging build is ready for UX sign-off. :thumbsup:
